subject.title: feat(config): coerce whole-value ${VAR} JSON arrays/objects in env substitution

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `${VAR:json}` as the supported generic syntax for environment-backed array and object config values?
rationale: Code review supports the implementation, but it cannot authorize a permanent config-language modifier and persistence compatibility obligation without maintainer intent.

options.title: Close pending sponsorship
options.body: Close this technically sound proposal and reopen or request a refreshed implementation if a maintainer later sponsors the config-language direction.

options.title: Sponsor and adopt
options.body: Explicitly accept `${VAR:json}` as a public contract and proceed through normal exact-head merge validation.

options.title: Keep grammar unchanged
options.body: Decline a generic modifier and retain string substitution or narrower field-specific mechanisms for structured values.

recommendation.title: Close pending sponsorship
recommendation.body: Close this technically sound proposal and reopen or request a refreshed implementation if a maintainer later sponsors the config-language direction.

likelyOwner.reason: The available review and history evidence points to him as the strongest decision owner across the config parser, preservation, and IO contract.
